cfg.title: Configuration
cfg.hint.liveVsRestart: Most settings apply immediately after saving. Already-loaded models keep their previous settings until reloaded. Only host/port require a full service restart.
cfg.field.gpuMemoryCeiling: GPU memory ceiling (sum of all engines)
cfg.field.defaultModel: Default model (used when a request has no "model")

cost.title: Cost Tracking
cost.disclaimer: Purely fictional cost comparison: the local model runs for free - this estimates what the same tokens would have cost via the Claude Sonnet 5 API, for reference. Adjust rates per model in the Config Editor.
cost.hint.pricedRequests: Requests without exact token usage show no cost
cost.hint.noUsage: No exact token usage for this request (e.g. streaming without stream_options.include_usage) - no cost shown
cost.hint.soFarOutputOnly: Live estimate from streamed tokens so far - output only, prompt cost not yet known
cost.confirm.resetAll: Delete ALL cost records? This cannot be undone.
help.poolBudget.title: Pool Memory Budget
help.poolBudget.body: Shows how much of the configured GPU memory budget (gpu_memory_ceiling) is currently claimed by all loaded models together - the SUM of each engine's gpu_memory_utilization value, not a live measurement of actual memory usage. If loading a new model would exceed this limit, the longest-idle model is automatically evicted (unless it currently has an active request).
help.kvCache.title: KV Cache
help.kvCache.body: How full this engine's KV cache (key-value cache) currently is - the memory where the model keeps track of every token in the context while generating. Comes directly from vLLM's own metrics. As this approaches 100%, vLLM can no longer accept new requests immediately and has to queue them.
help.avgTtft.title: Avg TTFT (Engine)
help.avgTtft.body: Average Time-To-First-Token of this engine across all requests it has served so far: the time from a request arriving at the engine to the first generated token (prompt processing). Comes directly from vLLM's own metrics, not calculated by this dashboard.
help.avgMsPerTok.title: Avg ms/Tok (Engine)
help.avgMsPerTok.body: Average time per generated token (time-per-output-token) across all requests this engine has served so far - the inverse of tokens/second generation speed. Comes directly from vLLM's own metrics.
help.tokensPromptGen.title: Tokens (Prompt/Gen.)
help.tokensPromptGen.body: Total number of prompt tokens processed / tokens generated by this engine since it started - summed across ALL requests it has served, not just the most recent one. Comes directly from vLLM's own counters and resets when the engine is unloaded.
help.requestsEngine.title: Requests (Running/Waiting)
help.requestsEngine.body: How many requests this engine is actively processing right now (running) vs. waiting for free capacity (waiting) - vLLM's own request queue, taken directly from its metrics. Thanks to continuous batching, several requests can be "running" at the same time.
help.phase.title: Phase
help.phase.body: What the model is currently doing for this request: 🥶 still loading (cold start) → ⏳ processing the prompt (no output yet) → 💭 thinking (reasoning models) / 🔧 calling a tool / ✍️ generating the answer. "since Xs" shows how long the current phase has been running. Hover the badge to see a timeline of all phase changes so far.
help.loadTime.title: Load Time
help.loadTime.body: How long this request had to wait until the requested model was ready - e.g. because of a cold start, or because another model first had to be evicted to make room. Close to 0 if the model was already warm.
help.ttft.title: TTFT
help.ttft.body: Time-To-First-Token: the time from "model ready" to the first generated token of this specific request - pure prompt-processing time, not including any load time.
help.liveTokens.title: Live Tokens
help.liveTokens.body: Prompt / generated tokens for this one running request. The generated-side count is live but approximate (1 streamed chunk with content ≈ 1 token, not an exact tokenizer count) and also shown split out separately for thinking/reasoning tokens (only if the model has a reasoning_parser configured - see the Config Editor). The prompt side shows "–" until vLLM reports it - which only happens mid-stream if the client sent stream_options.include_usage, otherwise it becomes known only once the request finishes.
help.throughput.title: Throughput
help.throughput.body: Current generation speed of this running request in tokens per second, calculated live from the tokens streamed so far since the answer started (after load time/prompt processing).
help.rag.title: RAG
help.rag.body: Shows whether automatic server-side RAG kicked in for this request: the model has an "Auto-RAG collection" configured (Config Editor), so the last user message was searched against that collection and relevant matches were prepended as context - without the client having to do anything special. "–" means either no collection is configured for this model, or nothing relevant enough was found (below the minimum score).
help.cost.title: Cost
help.cost.body: Purely fictional comparison value: what these tokens would have cost via a cloud API (default: Claude Sonnet 5 pricing, adjustable per model in the Config Editor). Local operation is and remains free - see the dedicated Costs page (💰 Costs) for details, history, and pricing configuration.
help.requestTokens.title: Prompt/Completion Tokens
help.requestTokens.body: Exact prompt/completion token counts for this one completed request (not cumulative like "Tokens (Prompt/Gen.)" in the Loaded Models table). Only available if the response included a usage field - for streaming requests without stream_options.include_usage this stays empty.
help.ramUnified.title: RAM Usage (Unified Memory)
help.ramUnified.body: On this hardware (Grace Blackwell / GB10), CPU and GPU share the same physical memory (unified memory) - so RAM usage here also covers the memory needs of loaded models. There's no separate VRAM display on this system.
help.cfg_host.title: Host
help.cfg_host.body: The IP address or hostname the vLLM Manager server itself listens on (not the individual model engines) - usually 127.0.0.1 for local-only access, or 0.0.0.0 to accept connections from other machines on the network.
help.cfg_port.title: Port
help.cfg_port.body: The TCP port the vLLM Manager server listens on - this is the port clients like VS Code or curl connect to, e.g. http://host:port/v1/chat/completions.
help.cfg_engineHost.title: Engine Host
help.cfg_engineHost.body: The host the individual vLLM engine processes bind to - normally localhost, since the manager talks to them directly and they aren't meant to be reachable from outside.
help.cfg_enginePort.title: Engine Base Port
help.cfg_enginePort.body: The port assigned to the first engine that gets started. Additional engines running at the same time (hot pool) automatically get the next free ports above this one.
help.cfg_hfHome.title: HF Home
help.cfg_hfHome.body: The directory where downloaded models are cached, in HuggingFace's own cache folder structure (same idea as the HF_HOME environment variable). Determines how much disk space downloads use and where.
help.cfg_vllmBin.title: vLLM Binary
help.cfg_vllmBin.body: Path to the vllm executable used to start engines. Leave empty to auto-detect it (PATH / active virtualenv) - only needed if you have multiple vLLM installations or a non-standard setup.
help.cfg_apiKeyEnabled.title: Require API key
help.cfg_apiKeyEnabled.body: When enabled, every request except /health must include a valid "Authorization: Bearer <key>" header - this dashboard included (you'll be prompted for the key once per browser session).
help.cfg_apiKeyKey.title: Key
help.cfg_apiKeyKey.body: The secret value clients must send as the bearer token. Only matters while "Require API key" above is enabled.
help.cfg_maxConcurrentModels.title: Max concurrent models
help.cfg_maxConcurrentModels.body: How many models may stay loaded in GPU memory at the same time (the "hot pool"). Requesting a model beyond this limit evicts the least-recently-used one first (unless it has an active request).
help.cfg_gpuMemoryCeiling.title: GPU memory ceiling
help.cfg_gpuMemoryCeiling.body: Upper bound (0-1, fraction of total VRAM) for the SUM of gpu_memory_utilization across all currently loaded engines. Keeps the hot pool from trying to load more models than actually fit in memory.
help.cfg_idleTimeout.title: Idle timeout
help.cfg_idleTimeout.body: Seconds without a request after which a model is automatically unloaded to free GPU memory. Empty = never unload automatically (the model stays loaded until manually unloaded, evicted for another model, or the service restarts).
help.cfg_startupTimeout.title: Startup timeout
help.cfg_startupTimeout.body: Maximum time in seconds to wait for a cold start (loading a model) to finish before giving up and reporting it as failed.
help.cfg_defaultModel.title: Default model
help.cfg_defaultModel.body: Used whenever an incoming request doesn't specify a "model" field - handy for clients/tools that always expect exactly one fixed model to be available.
help.cfg_autoReloadLastModel.title: Auto-reload last used model
help.cfg_autoReloadLastModel.body: On service restart, automatically reloads whichever model was last active, in the background, without blocking the server from accepting other requests in the meantime.
help.cfg_defaultServeArgs.title: Default Serve Args
help.cfg_defaultServeArgs.body: Fallback values used for any model that doesn't set its own GPU memory utilization / max model length below - saves repeating the same values on every model.
help.cfg_defaultGpuMemUtil.title: Default GPU memory utilization
help.cfg_defaultGpuMemUtil.body: Fallback for a model's own "GPU memory utilization" field when left empty.
help.cfg_defaultMaxModelLen.title: Default max model length
help.cfg_defaultMaxModelLen.body: Fallback for a model's own "Max model length" field when left empty.
help.cfg_pricing.title: Cost Tracking
help.cfg_pricing.body: Purely fictional prices used only to compare local usage against what the same tokens would have cost on a cloud API (see the Costs page) - default matches standard Claude Sonnet 5 pricing. Has no effect whatsoever on actual (free) local operation. Overridable per model further down.
help.cfg_pricingInput.title: Input $ / MTok
help.cfg_pricingInput.body: Fictional price per 1 million input (prompt) tokens, used only for the cost comparison on the Costs page.
help.cfg_pricingOutput.title: Output $ / MTok
help.cfg_pricingOutput.body: Fictional price per 1 million output (generated + reasoning) tokens, used only for the cost comparison on the Costs page.
help.cfg_ragEnabled.title: Enable RAG
help.cfg_ragEnabled.body: Master switch for the whole RAG feature (document storage, search, and automatic per-model RAG). When off, none of the settings below have any effect and RAG-related endpoints return an error.
help.cfg_qdrantHost.title: Qdrant Host
help.cfg_qdrantHost.body: Address of the Qdrant vector database server that stores the embeddings for all RAG collections.
help.cfg_qdrantPort.title: Qdrant Port
help.cfg_embeddingModel.title: Embedding model
help.cfg_embeddingModel.body: Which registered model (must have task: "embed") is used to turn text into vectors, both for storing documents and for searching. Runs like any other model in the hot pool, loaded on demand.
help.cfg_defaultCollection.title: Default collection
help.cfg_defaultCollection.body: Which collection manual RAG actions (the RAG page / API) fall back to when none is explicitly specified. Has no effect on automatic per-model RAG - each model there uses its own configured "Auto-RAG collection" (further down).
help.cfg_chunkSize.title: Chunk size (chars)
help.cfg_chunkSize.body: Maximum length of a single text chunk when splitting a document for storage, in characters. Larger chunks give more context per match but make search less precise.
help.cfg_chunkOverlap.title: Chunk overlap (chars)
help.cfg_chunkOverlap.body: How many characters consecutive chunks share with each other, so information near a chunk boundary doesn't get cut off from its surrounding context.
help.cfg_autoRagTopK.title: Auto-RAG: matches per request
help.cfg_autoRagTopK.body: How many of the most relevant chunks get automatically prepended as context to a chat request. Applies only to automatic per-model RAG (see "Auto-RAG collection" on each model further down) - not to manual searches via the RAG page/API, which take their own top_k per request.
help.cfg_autoRagMinScore.title: Auto-RAG: minimum relevance score
help.cfg_autoRagMinScore.body: Matches below this similarity score (0-1) are discarded and never injected as context - keeps clearly irrelevant results from cluttering the prompt when nothing useful was found.
help.cfg_lessonsLearnedCollection.title: Lessons Learned collection
help.cfg_lessonsLearnedCollection.body: Which collection the remember_lesson/search_lessons MCP tools use (see .vscode/mcp.json) to store and look up solved mistakes/corrections - kept separate from the default collection so lessons don't get mixed in with regular documents. Created automatically on first use, like any other collection.
help.cfg_lessonsLearnedAutoInject.title: Auto-inject Lessons Learned into every request
help.cfg_lessonsLearnedAutoInject.body: Safety net in addition to the MCP tools: when on, the Lessons Learned collection is automatically searched and injected as context on every request to a model with an Auto-RAG collection set - even if the agent (e.g. Qwen in VS Code) never calls search_lessons itself. Uses the same Auto-RAG top-k/min-score settings above.
help.cfg_modelName.title: Model name / path
help.cfg_modelName.body: The HuggingFace repo ID or local filesystem path to the model files - exactly what a client sends as "model" in its request.
help.cfg_modelEnabled.title: Enabled
help.cfg_modelEnabled.body: Disabled models stay in this list but can't be loaded or served - useful to temporarily hide a model (e.g. one that's broken or being replaced) without deleting its configuration.
help.cfg_task.title: Task
help.cfg_task.body: "generate" for normal chat/text models, "embed" for embedding models (used by the RAG system to turn text into vectors - see the RAG section above).
help.cfg_maxModelLen.title: Max model length
help.cfg_maxModelLen.body: The context window size in tokens for this model (passed to vLLM as --max-model-len). Larger values need more GPU memory for the KV cache.
help.cfg_gpuMemUtil.title: GPU memory utilization
help.cfg_gpuMemUtil.body: Fraction of GPU memory (0-1) this specific model's engine is allowed to reserve for itself. Empty = fall back to the Default Serve Args value above.
help.cfg_maxTokens.title: Max output tokens
help.cfg_maxTokens.body: Caps generation length only when the client itself doesn't request a max_tokens value - protects against runaway or repeating generations without limiting normal replies that set their own limit.
help.cfg_ragCollection.title: Auto-RAG collection
help.cfg_ragCollection.body: If set, every chat request to this model automatically searches this collection for relevant context and prepends it - the client doesn't need to support anything special. Requires RAG to be enabled with an embedding model configured (see the RAG section above).
help.cfg_repetitionPenalty.title: Repetition penalty
help.cfg_repetitionPenalty.body: Only applied when the client itself doesn't set repetition_penalty. Values above 1.0 penalize already-generated tokens, reducing the chance of runaway repetition loops (common with smaller reasoning models). Try 1.1-1.3 if a model tends to get stuck.
help.cfg_repetitionDetection.title: Detect and abort repetition loops
help.cfg_repetitionDetection.body: Watches the live response stream and aborts the request as soon as the same text keeps repeating verbatim - shows up in Active/Recent Requests as "Aborted (loop)". Only works for streamed requests. Disable only if a model is expected to legitimately repeat text (e.g. structured/repetitive output).
help.cfg_toolCallParser.title: Tool call parser
help.cfg_toolCallParser.body: vLLM's internal parser name for recognizing tool/function calls in this model's output - depends on the model family (see vLLM's documentation for supported values). Leave empty if the model doesn't support tool calling.
help.cfg_reasoningParser.title: Reasoning parser
help.cfg_reasoningParser.body: vLLM's internal parser name for splitting off the model's thinking process (e.g. <think>...</think>) into its own reasoning_content field instead of mixing it into the normal response text.
help.cfg_autoToolChoice.title: Enable auto tool choice
help.cfg_autoToolChoice.body: Lets the model decide itself whether and which tool to call, without the client having to explicitly set tool_choice. Requires a matching Tool call parser above.
help.cfg_vision.title: Vision
help.cfg_vision.body: Marks the model as vision-capable, purely for display (dashboard badges/icons) - doesn't change any actual server startup parameters.
help.cfg_pricingInputOverride.title: Cost tracking: input $/MTok override
help.cfg_pricingInputOverride.body: Overrides the global default input price just for this model, e.g. for a noticeably larger/smaller model. Empty = use the global default above.
help.cfg_pricingOutputOverride.title: Cost tracking: output $/MTok override
help.cfg_pricingOutputOverride.body: Overrides the global default output price just for this model. Empty = use the global default above.
help.cfg_hfToken.title: HF token
help.cfg_hfToken.body: Personal HuggingFace access token, only needed to download gated or private models. Stored in plain text in config.json - leave empty for public models.
help.cfg_extraArgs.title: Extra args
help.cfg_extraArgs.body: Additional command-line flags passed to vllm serve for this model, one flag/value per line (e.g. --foo on one line, then bar on the next) - for anything not covered by a dedicated field above.
help.cfg_notes.title: Notes
help.cfg_notes.body: Free-text notes, purely informational - shown e.g. in the model info tooltip on the main dashboard. Has no effect on how the model runs.
